newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two bombs hit targets in Corsica, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Two bombs hit targets in Corsica, no injuries.

text.p: Bombs rocked a state employment agency and a bar in Corsica overnight, causing damage but no injuries, officials said on Wednesday.

The first explosion late on Tuesday shattered the windows and damaged the employment office in Ile Rousse in the north of the French Mediterranean island. No one claimed responsibility for the explosion.

Over an hour later, a small bomb damaged the metal shutter of the Le Rallye bar in the island capital Ajaccio in the south. No one claimed responsibility but police found the words "Danger, mine, Arabs Out" scrawled on a wall.
Paris anti-terrorism magistrates have launched a probe into six suspected guerrillas following an upsurge in separatist violence, chiefly directed at government buildings.

Four Corsicans were placed in preventive detention and two freed on bail. All were suspected members or sympathisers of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing, which called off a shaky truce in mid-August.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe has repeatedly pledged to crack down on Corsican guerrillas pushing for greater autonomy from Paris, but few have been detained.
